clue.text: Game commander advanced position

parts.note: bridge is a card game
a head is a leader or person in command

explanation.surface: A games-playing general takes up a forward post.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridgehead is a forward foothold seized in enemy territory, an advanced military post.

clue.text: Independent religious group following bishop, creating schism

definitions.note: a verb phrase meaning splitting in two, matching the verb answer once read as 'create a schism'

indicators.note: the independent religious group comes after the bishop, so the bishop's letter goes first

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a sect is a breakaway religious group

explanation.surface: A breakaway church faction formed under a bishop splits the faithful.
explanation.definitionFit: To divide something into two parts is to cause a split, a schism, within it.

clue.text: In LA, professional killer in charge upset celebrity

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the word for celebrity is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: a big name is a celebrity

explanation.surface: A Los Angeles hitman, put in charge, topples a celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: American slang for a contract killer is a cool-headed hitman, hence 'In LA' marking the US usage.

clue.text: Take a walking holiday? Then Mrs May might do this!

definitions.meaning: literally heading out to the rural countryside for a ramble
the British idiom for a prime minister calling a general election; Theresa May did so in 2017

explanation.surface: A rambling break in the hills, the sort of thing a prime minister fancies.
explanation.walkthrough: Theresa May was the UK prime minister who called a snap general election in 2017; the British phrase for that is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom literally means a countryside trip and figuratively means a premier calling a national poll.

clue.text: Most Irish dancing is random

indicators.note: dancing letters move about, so the words Most Irish are rearranged

explanation.surface: Most Irish dancing is haphazard, says a sniffy critic.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done haphazardly, without aim or plan, is chancy and arbitrary.

clue.text: Characters in Sierra estate overturned cruising?

indicators.note: in a down clue, overturned means the hidden run is read from the bottom up
the letters sit inside the words Sierra estate

explanation.surface: A query about a car's letters on a Ford Sierra estate that has rolled over.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that cruising here is sailing on the ocean, not driving a Sierra estate car.
explanation.definitionFit: A passenger cruising is out on the ocean aboard ship, away from land.

clue.text: Fellow feeling secure?

definitions.meaning: a tie of shared sympathy between people
to fasten or stick firmly together

explanation.surface: A man asks whether he feels safe.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie of shared affection is a link between people; to fix firmly together is to glue or join.

clue.text: One manages old piece of poetry with little hesitation

definitions.note: a noun phrase, the person who manages

parts.note: a verse is a stanza or short poem
er is the small sound of a hesitating speaker

explanation.surface: A manager writes some old poetry, with the odd um and er.
explanation.definitionFit: A supervisor is the person in charge of running and checking others' work.

clue.text: Let off appointment college introduced

indicators.note: the college is brought into the middle of the appointment word

parts.note: a date is an arranged meeting
Eton is the famous English public school, formally Eton College

explanation.surface: A meeting arranged at a college is cancelled, the student let off.
explanation.definitionFit: To let off a bomb or firework is to set it off so it explodes.

clue.text: Artillery and cavalry unit's what's needed to restore power

parts.note: a battery is a unit of artillery guns
a charger is a cavalry horse, the unit a trooper rides

explanation.surface: Guns and horsemen together are what is needed to restore military strength.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that tops up a flat cell restores its electrical power.

clue.text: Fish was whiffy

definitions.meaning: gave off a smell, the British past tense of the verb to smell

explanation.surface: A fish that had gone off and stank.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a small edible fish, and also the British past form of 'smell', meaning gave off an odour.

clue.text: Time after trial to pen the last word in witness statement

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so the trial-and-time letters wrap around the last word
time is placed after the trial

parts.note: a test is a trial
amen is the word that ends a prayer

explanation.surface: A clerk, with time running out after a trial, writes the final words of a witness's statement.
explanation.definitionFit: A testament is evidence or proof, a formal declaration bearing witness to something.

clue.text: Cleaner concealing private part of book

indicators.note: the cleaner word hides the private inside it

parts.note: a char is a British cleaning lady, short for charwoman
Pte is the army abbreviation for the rank of private

explanation.surface: A cleaner hides a private section of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Books are divided into numbered sections, each a self-contained division of the text.

clue.text: Sit around in kind of knitwear made by craftsman

indicators.note: the turned-round word goes inside the knitwear

parts.note: Aran is a style of chunky cable-knit sweater from the Aran Islands of Ireland

indicators.note: around means the word sit is turned back to front

explanation.surface: Lounging about in a hand-knitted jumper made by a skilled craftsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A skilled manual worker who makes things by hand is a craftsman or maker.

clue.text: Drunk trembled, wine causing confusion

indicators.note: a drunk is all over the place, so the letters of trembled and wine are jumbled

explanation.surface: A drunk shakes, the wine leaving him baffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Bafflement and perplexity are states of not knowing what is going on.

clue.text: Showing embarrassment, put up with drummer catching daughter in bold action

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means the word for blushing is turned upside down

parts.note: red-faced, blushing with embarrassment

indicators.note: the drummer's name holds the daughter inside it

parts.note: Ringo Starr was the Beatles' drummer
D is the genealogy abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A blushing girl tolerates a drummer who traps his daughter in a daring act.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic phrase means heroic daring, brave deeds of an adventurous kind.

clue.text: Show anger over help for Egyptian city

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the word for a tantrum is flipped and read upwards

parts.note: to strop is British slang for to sulk or have a tantrum
aid means help

explanation.surface: Someone throws a tantrum about receiving help from Egypt.
explanation.walkthrough: A strop is British slang for a bad-tempered sulk.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Egyptian port at the northern end of the Suez Canal.

clue.text: Poet with gift for sorting out quibble

indicators.note: sorting out the letters of poet and gift means putting them in a new order

explanation.surface: A poet with a talent for tidying up a petty objection.
explanation.definitionFit: To argue over trivial details is to nitpick or cavil.

clue.text: Career he soon abandoned — it offers little competition

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and uncontrolled, so the letters of career he soon run riot

explanation.surface: A career was dropped quickly because it posed no challenge.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a contest with only one real contender, so there is barely a contest at all.

clue.text: Intended to separate the first knight from money

indicators.note: taking the knight away from the money word removes those letters

parts.note: finance means money or funds
N is the chess abbreviation for knight; the money word has two, and the first is taken

explanation.surface: A plan to divorce the leading knight from his fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intended' looks like a verb, but here it is the noun: the man someone is engaged to.
explanation.definitionFit: A man engaged to be married is his partner's betrothed, her husband-to-be.

clue.text: Words introducing unknown religious belief not generally accepted

parts.note: 'here's' is said when presenting someone, as in 'here's John'
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A speaker introduces a mysterious faith outside the mainstream.
explanation.definitionFit: An unorthodox belief that contradicts accepted church doctrine is a dissenting opinion.

clue.text: What's bust it? an iceberg's fragment

definitions.text: What's bust it? an iceberg's fragment

indicators.note: a fragment is a piece, here a run of letters lifted from inside the words

explanation.surface: A question about what wrecked a ship, answered by a chunk of iceberg.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: an iceberg sank the liner, and its name sits within the clue's words.
explanation.definitionFit: The White Star liner famously holed by an iceberg and sunk in 1912.

clue.text: Copyright article about Irish terrier

parts.note: C is the symbol for copyright

indicators.note: the article goes around the Irish abbreviation

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A copyrighted article about an Irish terrier.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a small, shaggy Scottish dog breed, one of the terrier family.

clue.text: Fancy silver collected by one working underground

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the silver is taken into the middle of the miner's letters

parts.note: to mine is to dig and work beneath the ground
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A miner gathers silver deep underground.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy or suppose is to picture something in the mind.

clue.text: Providing a fine crossing

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
fording is crossing a river through shallow water

explanation.surface: A good river crossing being supplied.
explanation.definitionFit: To give or supply something is to provide it, as in a view offering a vista.

clue.text: Name adopted by one famous acting style

indicators.note: the name is taken into the actor's surname

parts.note: Richard Gere is a famous actor

explanation.surface: A name taken on by a celebrated actor with a distinctive acting style.
explanation.definitionFit: A category or style of art, music or writing is its kind or type.

clue.text: Cheat, say, repelled magistrate

parts.note: to do someone is to swindle them

indicators.note: repelled means driven back, so the letters for say are reversed

parts.note: eg (for example) means say

explanation.surface: A judge drives off a would-be swindler.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief magistrate of Venice or Genoa was the elected ruler of the old republic.

clue.text: Tinier boys disorderly, being drunk

definitions.note: a noun phrase, the state of intoxication

indicators.note: disorderly means out of order, so the letters of tinier boys are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Smaller lads behaving badly after too much to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names the condition of intoxication, the opposite of sobriety.
